analysis.investment_thesis: Karnataka Bank is a classic asset-play/stalwart trading at 0.74x book and a PEG of ~0.33 (P/E 8.06 ÷ 5Y earnings CAGR 24.1%), making it statistically cheap. However, the growth story is weakening — FY25 profits slipped to ₹1,273 Cr from ₹1,307 Cr, and FCF collapsed to just ₹48 Cr, signaling the easy gains from post-COVID credit normalization are behind us.
key_strengths: Exceptional PEG of 0.33 using 5Y earnings CAGR of 24.1% — classic Lynch bargain on paper
Deep value: P/B 0.74 and forward P/E 6.06 suggest significant margin of safety on book assets
Equity base nearly doubled (₹5,971→₹12,589 Cr in 5 years), providing capital buffer for future loan growth
key_risks: Profit growth stalled in FY25 (₹1,307→₹1,273 Cr) — the 24% earnings CAGR was driven by one big step-change in FY23; organic growth is closer to 6-8%
Finance costs surging (₹5,000→₹5,703 Cr in one year) while revenue grew only 8.6% — NIM compression is a real threat
FCF crashed to ₹48 Cr in FY25 vs ₹570 Cr in FY24 — operating leverage is deteriorating fast
red_flags: Earnings CAGR optical distortion: FY23 profit nearly doubled (₹508→₹1,180 Cr) from credit cost release, not structural improvement
ROE of 11.1% is below my 12% minimum threshold for a bank to earn its cost of equity
Operating CF collapsed to ₹210 Cr in FY25 from ₹681 Cr in FY24 — volatile and trending down
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Karnataka Bank is a 100-year-old regional lender with a South Indian franchise that I'd classify as a stalwart-meets-asset-play. The headline numbers look seductive: P/E of 8, forward P/E of 6, and P/B of 0.74. The 5-year earnings CAGR of 24.1% produces a PEG ratio of 0.33 — the kind of number that makes a Lynch disciple reach for his checkbook. But I always dig into "what's the story," and here the story has a catch: that 24% earnings growth is heavily distorted by FY23's near-doubling of profits from ₹508 Cr to ₹1,180 Cr, which looks like credit cost normalization post-COVID, not a durable structural improvement. Revenue has only grown at 6.8% CAGR — that's the real underlying engine speed.

What worries me most is the deceleration signal in FY25: profits fell, FCF cratered to ₹48 Cr, and finance costs jumped ₹703 Cr while revenue grew ₹715 Cr — almost a 1:1 cost pass-through. ROE of 11.1% barely covers equity cost and hasn't crossed my 12% hurdle. The bank has no obvious moat — it competes with larger PSU banks and aggressive private lenders in Karnataka and coastal Karnataka markets. At this price, the downside is protected by the book value discount, but I don't see a compelling catalyst to re-rate this significantly higher without ROE expansion and a return to consistent profit growth. I'd hold if already owned, but there are better growth stories elsewhere at this price.
